summary: Self-hosted and cloud ecommerce platform (Adobe Commerce / Magento Open Source) for merchants.
access_note: Self-hosted per merchant: the store admin activates an integration to get keys/tokens. Magento Open Source is named in the docs; Adobe Commerce license cost not read.
blocker_note: Each merchant instance has its own base URL and an admin must create the integration or admin/IMS credentials.

evidence.quote: Use this token in applications to authorize an Admin user and access Admin-related APIs.
This method is a good choice for integrating with a third-party system that supports OAuth 1.0a.
After activating an integration (self activated), you can use the generated consumer key, consumer secret, access token, and access token secret
Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source allow developers to define web API resources and their permissions in the webapi.xml configuration file.
The Web API documentation is divided into three guides: REST, GraphQL, and Getting Started.
Adobe Commerce App Builder MCP server

notes: Official MCP found is the Adobe Commerce App Builder MCP server: IDE/developer tooling, not store data access. Fee for Adobe Commerce licence not verified either way, so access rests on self-activated integration text. SaaS (Commerce as a Cloud Service) uses IMS OAuth server-to-server, only linked on the auth page, not read.

review.reason: Open Source edition is named in the vendor docs and integrations are self-activated by the merchant admin; no page read states a license fee for API access. Pass-1 paid_plan was an unquoted inference.
Credentials come from an integration the store admin creates and activates on each instance.
